question.problem: By the multiplicative property of congruences, $92\cdot 93≡$
question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}92 & ≡18\cdot 5+2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡18\cdot 0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 93 & ≡18\cdot 5+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡18\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}92\cdot 93 & ≡2\cdot 3\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡5+1\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
92\cdot 93≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$
